attachement.q1: When your partner doesn't reply to a message for several hours, you…
attachement.q1a: Assume they're busy and calmly get on with your day.
attachement.q1b: Think about it a little, but manage to move on.
attachement.q1c: Check your phone regularly and start imagining scenarios.
attachement.q1d: Feel a growing anxiety and want to send another message.
attachement.q2: After an argument with your partner, your first instinct is to…
attachement.q2a: Take a moment to calm down, then come back and talk it through.
attachement.q2b: Try to understand their point of view, even when it's hard.
attachement.q2c: Withdraw and need a lot of time alone before talking again.
attachement.q2d: Seek reconciliation immediately, sometimes by giving in on everything.
attachement.q3: How would you describe your relationship to emotional intimacy?
attachement.q3a: I'm comfortable sharing my emotions and receiving theirs.
attachement.q3b: I manage overall, even if some emotions are hard to express.
attachement.q3c: I tend to keep my emotions to myself, too much closeness makes me uneasy.
attachement.q3d: I swing between an intense need for connection and an urge to run.
attachement.q4: When your partner is going through a hard time, you…
attachement.q4a: Are present and listen without trying to fix everything.
attachement.q4b: Try to help concretely, sometimes a little too much.
attachement.q4c: Aren't quite sure how to react and pull back.
attachement.q4d: Absorb their stress to the point that it affects your own state.
attachement.q5: In your past relationships, the recurring pattern was…
attachement.q5a: Stable, respectful relationships, even the ones that ended.
attachement.q5b: Ups and downs, but nothing really problematic.
attachement.q5c: I often ended up feeling smothered and pulling away.
attachement.q5d: I was afraid of being abandoned and held on too tightly.
attachement.q6: When your partner spends time with their friends without you…
attachement.q6a: Good! You enjoy your own time too.
attachement.q6b: It's normal, even if sometimes you'd like to be invited.
attachement.q6c: You much prefer having your own space anyway.
attachement.q6d: You feel a bit left out and need reassurance.
attachement.q7: Faced with an unresolved conflict in your relationship, you…
attachement.q7a: Come back to it calmly when the right moment comes.
attachement.q7b: Hope it will pass on its own, but agree to talk about it again.
attachement.q7c: Would rather not discuss it, conflict makes you very uncomfortable.
attachement.q7d: Think about it on a loop and struggle to let go until it's settled.
attachement.q8: How do you react when your partner gives you a sincere compliment?
attachement.q8a: You take it with pleasure and thank them naturally.
attachement.q8b: It touches you, even if you sometimes play it down.
attachement.q8c: You feel awkward and change the subject.
attachement.q8d: You doubt their sincerity or wonder if they want something.
attachement.q9: When you think about the future of your relationship, you feel…
attachement.q9b: Optimism, with a few normal questions.
attachement.q9c: A certain reserve, you'd rather not project too far ahead.
attachement.q9d: Anxiety at the thought that it could end.
attachement.q10: If your partner expresses a need different from yours…
attachement.q10a: You discuss it to find a compromise that suits you both.
attachement.q10b: You try to adapt, even if it's frustrating sometimes.
attachement.q10c: You struggle to understand why they don't think like you.
attachement.q10d: You're afraid this difference puts the relationship at risk.
attachement.q11: Your vision of the ideal couple is closest to…
attachement.q11a: Two independent people who choose each other every day.
attachement.q11b: A solid partnership with closeness and mutual support.
attachement.q11c: Two people who respect each other's space and freedom above all.
attachement.q11d: A total fusion where you share absolutely everything.
attachement.q12: When you sense your partner pulling away…
attachement.q12a: You give them space while staying available.
attachement.q12b: You calmly ask whether everything is alright.
attachement.q12c: You pull away too, it's more comfortable.
attachement.q12d: You panic inside and try to draw them back in.
attachement.q13: How do you handle vulnerability in your relationship?
attachement.q13a: Being vulnerable is a strength, I'm not afraid to show my cracks.
attachement.q13b: I try to be open, but some subjects stay difficult.
attachement.q13c: I rarely show vulnerability, I'd rather appear solid.
attachement.q13d: My vulnerability sometimes overflows: I cry easily, I fear being judged.
attachement.q14: If your partner forgets an important date (a birthday, an anniversary)…
attachement.q14a: You mention it without drama, people forget things.
attachement.q14b: You're disappointed but you put it in perspective fairly quickly.
attachement.q14c: You say nothing but you note it internally.
attachement.q14d: You take it as proof that they don't care enough about you.
attachement.q15: What role does jealousy play in your relationship?
attachement.q15a: Almost none, I trust my partner.
attachement.q15b: Rarely, and when it happens, I talk about it openly.
attachement.q15c: I don't show my jealousy, but it's there, hidden.
attachement.q15d: Jealousy sometimes consumes me and I can't control it.
attachement.q16: When you're stressed by work or life in general…
attachement.q16a: You talk to your partner about it and accept their support.
attachement.q16b: You share a little but keep some of it to yourself.
attachement.q16c: You close up, your partner can't really help.
attachement.q16d: You need your partner to be constantly there to reassure you.
attachement.q17: Your greatest fear in a romantic relationship is…
attachement.q17a: I don't have a dominant fear, every relationship is an adventure.
attachement.q17b: That routine sets in and the connection weakens.
attachement.q17c: Losing my independence or feeling trapped.
attachement.q17d: Being abandoned or not being loved enough.
attachement.q18: How would you describe your need for reassurance in a relationship?
attachement.q18a: Minimal, the trust is there, no need for constant validation.
attachement.q18b: Moderate, a kind word now and then feels good.
attachement.q18c: Low, grand declarations make me uncomfortable.
attachement.q18d: Intense, I often need to be told that everything is fine.
attachement.q19: If your partner had to travel alone for two weeks…
attachement.q19a: Great! You make the most of your own time and reunite happily after.
attachement.q19b: You'd miss them but you'd manage fine.
attachement.q19d: Two weeks without them? You dread that separation.
attachement.q20: Overall, in your current or past relationship, you feel…
attachement.q20a: Safe, loved and free to be yourself.
attachement.q20b: Pretty good, with ups and downs like everyone.
attachement.q20c: Sometimes a little confined or smothered by the other's expectations.
attachement.q20d: Often on edge, as if the relationship could tip over at any moment.
attachement.pf_secure_d: You have a secure attachment: you're comfortable with both intimacy and independence. You express your needs clearly, you trust your partner, and conflict doesn't threaten the bond you share.
attachement.pf_secure_a: Your emotional security is a real strength for your relationship. You can be a stabilising anchor for a partner with a more anxious or avoidant style, as long as you don't take on the whole emotional load by yourself.
attachement.pf_anxious_d: Your attachment leans anxious: you have an intense need for closeness and reassurance. The fear of abandonment can push you to over-analyse your partner's behaviour, to seek constant proof of love, and to feel destabilised by the smallest distance.
attachement.pf_anxious_a: Learn to self-soothe when the anxiety rises: breathing, grounding, writing down what you feel before reacting. And name your need for reassurance out loud rather than testing your partner, a request is always heard better than a test.
attachement.pf_avoidant_d: Your attachment leans avoidant: you value your independence highly. Emotional intimacy can feel intrusive, and your instinct when things get intense is to create distance, often without meaning to hurt anyone.
attachement.pf_avoidant_a: Practise staying present in moments of intimacy rather than pulling away automatically. And when you need space, say so instead of taking it silently: a stated need protects the bond, a silent withdrawal damages it.
attachement.pf_disorganized_d: Your attachment combines anxious and avoidant traits: you swing between a strong desire for connection and a fear of intimacy. You may draw closer then push away, which is exhausting for you and confusing for your partner.
attachement.pf_disorganized_a: This profile benefits particularly from support: therapy helps make sense of these contradictory movements, which usually have their roots well before your current relationship. In the meantime, naming the swing out loud already takes a lot of pressure off your partner.
